newsitem.title: UK: Abbey bids up to 1.4 bln stg for ScotAm.
newsitem.headline: Abbey bids up to 1.4 bln stg for ScotAm.

text.p: British retail banking group Abbey National Plc said on Friday that it has made a bid of between 1.1 billion to 1.4 billion pounds ($2.27 billion) for life insurance company Scottish Amicable.

Scottish Amicable, which earlier this month announced plans to shed its mutual status, has rejected the bid. The offer entails a minimum of 400 million pounds to policyholders and an immediate investment into the funds of with-profit policyholders of between 700 million to one billion pounds.

Abbey National, the UK's fifth largest bank, said the immediate offer of 400 million pounds would be in either cash or shares with the bulk of this going to the Scottish Amicable's existing 1.1 million with-profit policyholders.

"We believe this offer will by very attractive to Scottish Amicable policyholders, providing them with immediate value and the long-term security of being part of one of the UK's strongest financial groups," Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch said in a statement.

The second element of the offer would see Abbey National invest between 700 million and one billion pounds into the with-profits fund, where the policyholder is entitled to a share of the profits from the growth of the fund. "The range is wide because it is very difficult to calculate embedded value until you look deep into the books," an Abbey National spokesman told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Scottish Amicable said the approach from Abbey was vague and it was unclear how Abbey National was valuing the group. The insurer, based in Stirling, Scotland, said it intends to publish in 10 days time detailed proposals about a twin-phased transformation, involving losing its mutual status on May 1 and a 1.0 billion pound flotation in three to five years time.

"The start of a growth phase is the wrong time in the cycle for policyholders to put their businesss on the market," said Sandy Stewart, chairman of Scottish Amicable. When asked if the door was still open for talks with Abbey, a spokesman for the Scottish Amicable said the board has a fiduciary duty to act in the best interests of policy holders.
But he said the company's existing twin-phased proposals were still considered to be the best deal for policyholders.
